title: China: Geography, Sacred Mountains & Megacities
description: A 60-question grand master assessment exploring the Tibetan Plateau & Everest, the Yangtze & Three Gorges, the Yellow River, the Great Wall (21,196 km), Guilin & Zhangjiajie, megacities, the Taklamakan Desert, sacred mountains, and giant pandas.

questions.question: What massive, high-altitude plateau in southwestern China covering 2.5 million square kilometers is called the Roof of the World and the Third Pole?
questions.explanation: With an average elevation exceeding 4,500 meters, the Tibetan Plateau is the world highest and largest plateau, containing the largest concentration of ice outside the polar caps.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in the world, rising 8,848.86 meters on the international border between China (Tibet) and Nepal?
questions.explanation: Known in Tibetan as Qomolangma (Holy Mother), the summit represents the highest elevation on Earth, formed by the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

questions.question: Which national nature reserve on the Tibetan Plateau protects the headwaters of Asia three greatest rivers: the Yangtze, Yellow, and Lancang (Mekong)?
questions.explanation: Sanjiangyuan is China largest national park, providing crucial freshwater for nearly one billion people downstream and protecting the endangered Tibetan antelope (chiru).

questions.question: What is the deepest and longest terrestrial canyon on Earth, carved by the Yarlung Tsangpo River as it cuts around Mount Namcha Barwa in Tibet?
questions.explanation: Reaching a maximum depth of 6,009 meters and stretching 504 kilometers, the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon is more than three times deeper than the US Grand Canyon.

questions.question: What monumental 13-story fortress-palace in Lhasa served as the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas from 1649 to 1959, perched atop Red Hill at 3,700 meters?
questions.explanation: Constructed by the 5th Dalai Lama, the Potala Palace contains over 1,000 rooms and the gold-encrusted stupa tombs of eight past Dalai Lamas.

questions.question: What is the official joint surveyed summit elevation in meters above sea level of Mount Everest (Mount Qomolangma)?
questions.explanation: In December 2020, Chinese and Nepalese surveying authorities jointly announced the official elevation of Mount Everest as 8,848.86 meters (rounded to 8,849 m).

questions.question: What is the longest river in Asia and third longest on Earth, flowing 6,300 kilometers from the glaciers of Tibet into the East China Sea at Shanghai?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze (Long River) drains one-fifth of China land area, generating roughly forty percent of the country total Gross Domestic Product.

questions.question: What is the world largest hydroelectric power station by installed electrical capacity (22,500 megawatts), built across the Yangtze in Hubei Province?
questions.explanation: The concrete gravity dam spans 2.3 kilometers across the river, creating a 660-kilometer reservoir that raised river navigation to Chongqing.

questions.question: What three famous scenic river gorges on the upper Yangtze stretch for 120 miles between Chongqing and Yichang?
questions.explanation: The Three Gorges are flanked by sheer thousand-meter limestone cliffs, celebrated in Chinese classical poetry and ink-wash landscape paintings for dynasties.

questions.question: What fertile, mineral-rich lowland basin in southwestern China surrounded by high mountains is nicknamed the Red Basin or Land of Abundance?
questions.explanation: The Sichuan Basin is home to over one hundred million people, watered by the ancient 3rd-century BCE Dujiangyan irrigation system near Chengdu.

questions.question: What is the busiest container seaport in the world, located at the mouth of the Yangtze River on Hangzhou Bay in eastern China?
questions.explanation: Shanghai Yangshan Deep-Water Port is connected to the mainland by the 32.5-kilometer Donghai Bridge, handling over forty-seven million shipping containers annually.

questions.question: What is the total length in kilometers of the Yangtze River (Chang Jiang), the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze River stretches for approximately 6,300 kilometers from the Tanggula Mountains in Qinghai to the East China Sea.

questions.question: What 5,464-kilometer river is revered as the Cradle of Chinese Civilization, named for the heavy load of yellow silt it carries across northern China?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River carries over 1.6 billion tons of silt annually from the Loess Plateau, giving the Yellow Sea its distinctive muddy golden coloration.

questions.question: What massive 640,000-square-kilometer plateau in northern China is covered by deep windblown deposits of fine, highly fertile yellow dust (loess)?
questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau was the heartland of early Chinese agriculture, where millions of people traditionally lived in cave dwellings carved into cliffs (yaodong).

questions.question: What is the largest waterfall on the Yellow River, where the river narrows dramatically into a 20-meter canyon of golden, boiling yellow rapids?
questions.explanation: Hukou (Teapot Spout) Waterfall changes in height and character with seasonal river flows, famous for yellow mists depicted on the Chinese 50-yuan currency note.

questions.question: Which ancient imperial capital of Shaanxi was the starting point of the Silk Road and site of the 8,000-statue Terracotta Army of Emperor Qin Shi Huang?
questions.explanation: Xi'an was the capital for thirteen dynasties over a millennium, protected by the world most complete surviving ancient city wall spanning fourteen kilometers.

questions.question: What massive northern U-shaped bend of the Yellow River loops through Inner Mongolia, enclosing the Ordos desert plateau?
questions.explanation: The Ordos Loop was a strategic frontier boundary between Chinese agrarian civilization and nomadic steppe confederations like the Xiongnu and Mongols.

questions.question: What is the total length in kilometers of the Yellow River (Huang He), the second longest river in China?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River flows for 5,464 kilometers from the Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai to the Bohai Sea in Shandong.

questions.question: According to official comprehensive archaeological surveys by China State Administration of Cultural Heritage, what is the total length of all Great Wall sections built across dynasties?
questions.explanation: This survey encompasses walls, trenches, watchtowers, and natural defensive barriers constructed by the Qin, Han, Tang, and Ming dynasties across fifteen provinces.

questions.question: Which iconic, well-preserved section of the Ming Dynasty Great Wall seventy kilometers northwest of Beijing was the first section opened to tourists in 1957?
questions.explanation: Badaling features massive stone watchtowers and crenellated battlements guarding the strategic Juyongguan Pass into the Beijing plain.

questions.question: What fortress at the western terminus of the Ming Dynasty Great Wall in Gansu is known as the First and Greatest Pass Under Heaven?
questions.explanation: Built in 1372 along the Hexi Corridor, Jiayuguan guarded the narrow desert passage between the snow-capped Qilian Mountains and the Black Mountain.

questions.question: What fortress at the eastern coastal terminus of the Ming Great Wall in Hebei is where the wall meets the Bohai Sea at Old Dragon Head (Laolongtou)?
questions.explanation: In 1644, Ming general Wu Sangui opened the gates of Shanhaiguan to the invading Manchu army, leading directly to the establishment of the Qing Dynasty in Beijing.

questions.question: Which UNESCO World Heritage complex of 492 rock-cut cave temples near Dunhuang on the ancient Silk Road preserves a millennium of Buddhist murals and manuscripts?
questions.explanation: Discovered in 1900 by Daoist priest Wang Yuanlu, Cave 17 (the Library Cave) contained over 50,000 ancient manuscripts, textiles, and the 868 CE Diamond Sutra.

questions.question: What is the total official surveyed length in thousands of kilometers of all Great Wall structures built throughout Chinese history?
questions.explanation: Official surveys confirm the total combined length of all historical wall sections is 21,196 kilometers (rounded to 21k km).

questions.question: What world-famous picturesque river in Guangxi winds eighty-three kilometers past towering cone karst limestone peaks between Guilin and Yangshuo?
questions.explanation: The reflection of the karst peaks in the crystal waters of the Li River is depicted on the reverse side of the Chinese 20-yuan banknote.

questions.question: Which national forest park in Hunan Province features over 3,000 quartz-sandstone pillars that served as the visual prototype for the floating Hallelujah Mountains in Avatar?
questions.explanation: Located in the Wulingyuan Scenic Area, the Southern Sky Column was officially renamed Avatar Hallelujah Mountain following the blockbuster film release.

questions.question: What is the tallest outdoor glass sightseeing elevator in the world, built into the cliff face of a 326-meter sandstone precipice in Zhangjiajie?
questions.explanation: The glass double-decker elevator ascends the vertical sandstone cliff in just sixty-six seconds, carrying up to fifty passengers per cabin.

questions.question: What spectacular geological stone forest in Yunnan Province covers 400 square kilometers of towering eroded limestone pillars resembling a petrified forest?
questions.explanation: Formed 270 million years ago from ancient seabed dissolution, Shilin is celebrated in the traditional Ashima folklore of the indigenous Yi (Sani) people.

questions.question: What is the largest waterfall in China and East Asia, plunging seventy-eight meters across a limestone cliff on the Baishui River in Guizhou?
questions.explanation: Behind the rushing torrent of Huangguoshu lies the 134-meter Shuiliandong (Water Curtain Cave), allowing visitors to walk directly behind the roaring cataract.

questions.question: What is the total height in meters of the Bailong outdoor glass cliff elevator in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park?
questions.explanation: The Bailong Elevator holds the Guinness World Record for the tallest outdoor glass elevator on Earth at 326 meters.

questions.question: What is the national capital of the People Republic of China, centered on Tiananmen Square and the 9,999-room Forbidden City imperial palace?
questions.explanation: Beijing was the capital of the Ming and Qing dynasties and modern China, home to the Summer Palace, Temple of Heaven, and 2008/2022 Olympic venues.

questions.question: Which ultramodern financial and commercial skyscraper district in Shanghai sits directly across the Huangpu River from the historic colonial Bund?
questions.explanation: Lujiazui features iconic megatall architecture including the 632-meter Shanghai Tower (second tallest building on Earth), the Oriental Pearl Tower, and Jin Mao Tower.

questions.question: What massive urban megalopolis in Guangdong Province encompassing Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and Macau is the world largest continuous urban agglomeration?
questions.explanation: Home to over eighty-six million people, the Greater Bay Area generates a regional GDP exceeding 1.9 trillion dollars, leading global high-tech and hardware manufacturing.

questions.question: Which directly administered municipality in southwest China on the upper Yangtze is the largest municipal city in the world by administrative area and population?
questions.explanation: Spanning 82,400 square kilometers (roughly the size of Austria) with thirty-two million residents, mountainous Chongqing is famous for spicy Sichuan hot pot.

questions.question: What 55-kilometer bridge-tunnel sea crossing opened in 2018 is the longest open-sea fixed link in the world, connecting Hong Kong, Zhuhai, and Macau across the Pearl River estuary?
questions.explanation: The crossing includes three cable-stayed bridges, an undersea tunnel, and four artificial islands designed to withstand magnitude 8.0 earthquakes and super typhoons.

questions.question: What is the total length in kilometers of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao sea-bridge and tunnel crossing across the Pearl River estuary?
questions.explanation: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge spans 55 kilometers, making it the longest sea-crossing bridge-tunnel system in the world.

questions.question: What immense 337,000-square-kilometer shifting sand desert in Xinjiang is nicknamed the Sea of Death or Place of No Return?
questions.explanation: Surrounded by the Tian Shan, Pamir, and Kunlun mountains, the Taklamakan is traversed by the modern Tarim Desert Highway built on top of shifting barchan dunes.

questions.question: What is the lowest natural point on land in China, an endorheic salt lake in Xinjiang that sits 154 meters below sea level?
questions.explanation: The Turpan Depression is one of the hottest and driest places on Earth, famous for the Flaming Mountains and subterranean Karez water channel systems.

questions.question: Which ancient Silk Road oasis city in western Xinjiang near the Pamir Mountains is celebrated for its historic mudbrick Old City and bustling Sunday Livestock Market?
questions.explanation: Kashgar was the central junction where northern and southern branches of the Silk Road converged before caravans crossed high passes into Persia and India.

questions.question: What desert in Inner Mongolia contains the tallest stationary sand dunes on Earth, rising up to 500 meters high alongside over one hundred mysterious spring-fed lakes?
questions.explanation: Bilutu Peak in the Badain Jaran Desert rises 460 meters above its base (1,611 m elevation), often called the Mount Everest of Sand Dunes.

questions.question: Which dried-up nuclear test site basin and salt lake in southeastern Xinjiang was the former location of the mysterious wandering Lake Lop Nur and ancient Loulan Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Lop Nur is famous for its Ear of the Earth satellite appearance and the discovery of the remarkably preserved 3,800-year-old Caucasian Loulan Beauty mummy.

questions.question: How many meters below mean sea level is Ayding Lake in the Turpan Depression, the lowest point in China?
questions.explanation: Ayding Lake sits at 154 meters below sea level, the fourth lowest exposed dry land point on Earth after the Dead Sea, Lake Assal, and Sea of Galilee.

questions.question: Which sacred peak in Shandong Province is revered as the Eastern Peak and foremost of the Five Great Mountains of China (Wuyue), climbed by seventy-two Chinese emperors?
questions.explanation: Mount Tai has 6,660 stone steps ascending to the Jade Emperor Peak, where imperial sovereigns performed the sacred Feng and Shan sacrifice rituals.

questions.question: Which sheer granite mountain in Shaanxi Province, known as the Western Peak, is famous for having one of the world most thrilling cliffside plank walks?
questions.explanation: Mount Hua features five distinct peaks shaped like a five-petaled lotus flower, famous for Taoist monasteries and vertical chain-assisted rock stairways.

questions.question: Which UNESCO World Heritage mountain range in Anhui Province is celebrated for granite peaks, twisted Huangshan pine trees, hot springs, and a perpetual Sea of Clouds?
questions.explanation: Huangshan has inspired classic Chinese landscape painting (shan shui) for over a thousand years, featuring peaks like the Lotus Peak and Bright Summit.

questions.question: Which sacred Buddhist mountain in Sichuan Province is home to the 71-meter Leshan Giant Buddha carved directly out of a sandstone river cliff in the 8th century?
questions.explanation: Mount Emei is the sacred seat of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, while the nearby Leshan Buddha is the largest pre-modern carved stone Buddha in the world.

questions.question: Which mountain in Henan Province is home to the legendary Shaolin Monastery, the historical cradle of Chinese Chan (Zen) Buddhism and Shaolin Kung Fu?
questions.explanation: Founded in 495 CE, the Shaolin Temple on Mount Song features the Pagoda Forest, a cemetery containing over 240 ancient stone brick stupas of Buddhist masters.

questions.question: How many sacred Taoist mountains comprise the historic Five Great Mountains of China (Wuyue: Tai, Hua, Heng-Hunan, Heng-Shanxi, Song)?
questions.explanation: The Five Great Mountains of China correspond to the cardinal directions and center of traditional Chinese cosmology.

questions.question: Which global conservation icon and endemic Chinese mammal species inhabits the high-altitude misty bamboo forests of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu?
questions.explanation: Giant pandas feed almost exclusively on bamboo, eating up to thirty-eight kilograms daily, protected in China Giant Panda National Park.

questions.question: What percentage of the world remaining wild giant pandas live within the protected mountain bamboo reserves of Sichuan Province?
questions.explanation: Over 1,400 wild giant pandas (roughly three-quarters of the total wild population of 1,860) live in the Minshan and Qionglai mountain ranges of Sichuan.

questions.question: Which endangered primate species with striking golden-orange fur and blue-tinted faces lives in troops in the snowy temperate forests of the Qinling Mountains?
questions.explanation: Rhinopithecus roxellana survives harsh sub-zero winter temperatures by huddling together in large social family groups high in the forest canopy.

questions.question: What elusive big cat species, known as the Ghost of the Mountains, has sixty percent of its global wild population residing across the Tibetan Plateau in China?
questions.explanation: Sanjiangyuan and Qomolangma national parks contain vast rocky alpine habitats where snow leopards hunt blue sheep (bharal) and ibex.

questions.question: What critically endangered, near-extinct crocodilian species native to the lower Yangtze River basin is one of only two alligator species on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Chinese alligator (mud dragon) grows up to two meters long, spending winter in underground burrows, heavily protected by breeding centers in Anhui.

questions.question: What percentage of the world wild giant panda population inhabits the mountain forests of Sichuan Province in China?
questions.explanation: Approximately 75 percent of all wild giant pandas live across the protected bamboo reserves of Sichuan.

questions.question: Tying with the Russian Federation for the world record, how many sovereign countries share a direct terrestrial land border with the People Republic of China?
questions.explanation: China borders North Korea, Russia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Laos, and Vietnam.

questions.question: What is the largest provincial-level administrative division in China by geographical land area, covering over 1.66 million square kilometers in the northwest?
questions.explanation: Xinjiang accounts for one-sixth of China entire territory (larger than France, Germany, Spain, and the UK combined), bordering eight foreign nations.

questions.question: What is the most populous province in China, home to over 126 million residents and the manufacturing hub of the Pearl River Delta?
questions.explanation: Guangdong has been China economic powerhouse since the 1980s opening of Special Economic Zones like Shenzhen, generating over thirteen percent of China GDP.

questions.question: How many official direct-administered municipalities (equivalent to provinces) exist in China: Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and Chongqing?
questions.explanation: These four megacities report directly to the central government in Beijing, holding provincial-level administrative status.

questions.question: What is the total geographical area of China in square kilometers, ranking it as the third or fourth largest country in the world?
questions.explanation: China encompasses approximately 9.6 million square kilometers, spanning five geographical time zones (though unified under single Beijing Time UTC+8).

questions.question: How many sovereign foreign nations share a terrestrial land border with the People Republic of China, tying the world record?
questions.explanation: China shares land borders with fourteen sovereign nations, spanning over 22,000 kilometers of land frontier.
